subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should Telegram/ACP source turns fail closed, warn, suppress, or auto-recover when visible assistant text claims a mutating side effect but the run has no matching successful tool-call evidence?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the correct product behavior affects delivery semantics and compatibility across chat channels and ACP streaming modes.

options.title: Define verification and diagnostics first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the verification/fail-closed/warning policy and require live Telegram ACP proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to message-tool delivery only
options.body: Treat the remaining work as part of the message-tool-only fallback cluster and avoid broader completed-action verification for arbitrary tools.

options.title: Document as model/prompt responsibility
options.body: Close the core bug only if maintainers decide OpenClaw will not police claimed side effects beyond existing delivery modes and tool-failure diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Define verification and diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers choose the verification/fail-closed/warning policy and require live Telegram ACP proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the clearest recent owner signal for source-reply and private-final delivery policy changes that would frame the product decision.
